text.text: New Zealand’s white-ball captain Mitchell Santner is banking on home conditions to help his team counter India’s formidable batting line-up as the sides prepare for a demanding multi-format series, beginning with five T20Is on October 22.Earlier this year, India beat New Zealand 4-1 in their bilateral T20I series at home before defeating them in the T20 World Cup final, also on home soil. But Santner believes the change in conditions will give the Kiwis an opportunity to turn the tables.“We know how good India are,” Santner said during an interaction arranged by Sony Sports Network. “They’re so good at playing in their home conditions and on those grounds, and it’s the same for us. We know how to operate in New Zealand, so I think that gives us a little bit of an edge.”Santner, however, is wary of the damage India can inflict if the surfaces are flat and the boundaries short, conditions that have increasingly favoured aggressive batting in white-ball cricket. text.text: Red Bull have confirmed that Laurent Mekies will continue his role as Team Principal through 2031. Laurent Mekies has signed a long-term contract extension to remain as Red Bull's CEO and Team Principal, lasting through the 2031 season. The French engineer was promoted from Racing Bulls in July 2025 and led the Milton Keynes-based outfit through a challenging start to this year, which saw them drop behind their rivals under the new regulations. However, their consistent work over the course of 2026 – guided by Mekies – finally paid off as Max Verstappen secured back-to-back victories in Malaysia and Singapore, bringing Red Bull back into contention for regular wins. Charles Leclerc admits he missed a chance against Max Verstappen – but not the obvious one

text.text: When Charles Leclerc had a better start than Max Verstappen and claimed the inside line for Turn 1, many in the media centre thought the Monegasque should have held his ground to take the lead. However, Verstappen was on the outside, on the normal racing line that offered slightly more grip, and the Dutchman was prepared to take every risk. Verstappen had already told Autosport a day earlier that second or third place in the drivers' championship would mean nothing to him and that he simply wanted to go all-in for race victories. In other words, Verstappen was willing to risk everything, although that was not even the main reason why Leclerc was unable to complete the move. The reference points drivers use under braking – such as the 150-metre and 100-metre boards – are on the right-hand side approaching Turn 1, but Leclerc could not see them because he was alongside Verstappen. The Ferrari driver had to choose his braking point by instinct and tried to judge it as well as possible. text.text: Cristiano Ronaldo has shown his connection to Saudi Arabia with a gesture that carried added significance after a tense night in Riyadh. The Portuguese forward waved a scarf featuring the Saudi flag following Al-Nassr's 3-1 victory over FC Neftchi Fergana in the AFC Champions League Elite, reaffirming his bond with the country and its fans who welcomed him when his career was under scrutiny. There has also been speculation that he could end his playing career in Saudi Arabia. The match was delayed by an hour after an aerial missile alert and explosions were reported across the city. Yemen-based Houthi rebels launched ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh, while Saudi-led coalition forces intercepted and destroyed the incoming projectiles. The fixture went ahead once authorities confirmed the danger had passed. Ronaldo scored Al-Nassr's second goal in the 42nd minute, taking his career tally to 981 goals during the match in Riyadh. Despite the security concerns surrounding the fixture, Al-Nassr maintained their composure to secure a 3-1 win and claim three points in the continental competition. why: Internazionale beaten by Club Brugge at home

report.text: Club Brugge and their young forward Nicolò Tresoldi shocked Inter 4-3 at San Siro in the Champions League’s result of the night. Tresoldi, a 22-year-old Italian-born Germany Under-21s forward, scored the first three goals for the Belgian side. A Hakan Calhanoglu foul on Carlos Forbs resulted in a penalty which Tresoldi slotted in just before the half hour. Tresoldi picked up his second after capitalising on a blunder by the Inter keeper Josep Martínez and reacted faster than the Inter defence for the third with a quarter of an hour to go. Lautaro Martínez had given his team a lifeline just before the break after a move initiated by Marcus Thuram, followed by a Federico Dimarco back-heel assist. The Argentinian then gave the San Siro crowd hope again in the 81st minute by narrowing the score to 3-2, but Romeo Vermant once again exposed Inter’s defensive fragility by adding a fourth goal in the 87th minute. Ange-Yoan Bonny pulled a goal back for the home side in the third minute of stoppage time. reports.headline: Real Madrid produce a wild comeback against Roma: How did they do it again?
Real Madrid stun Roma after dramatic late comeback

report.text: José Mourinho enjoyed a Roma reunion to remember as Real Madrid completed an astonishing comeback by scoring three late goals to claim a 4-3 away win in the Champions League on Wednesday. Marten de Roon gave the hosts a deserved opener before Kylian Mbappé struck back on his 100th Champions League appearance to level the scores at the break. Two Donyell Malen strikes in the space of six minutes early in the second half seemed to take the game away from the 15-time European champions as Roma ran rampant. But Madrid scored three goals in the final six minutes, all stemming from corners, to turn the game on its head as Carlos Espí, Endrick and the former Roma defender Antonio Rüdiger struck at a stunned Stadio Olimpico. “You could say there were two games in one,” Mourinho said. “Roma were better in all aspects early on. When it was 3-1 everyone probably thought the game was over.” Mourinho was a popular figure as he led Roma to the Conference League title and Europa League final during two-and-a-half years in charge. reports.headline: 981st! Ronaldo Scores in Al Nassr’s 3-1 Win Over Neftchi as Portugal Suspension Row Continues
Why Ronaldo's Al Nassr AFC Champions League Elite match was delayed by an hour
Cristiano Ronaldo scores as Al-Nassr beat Neftchi after security delay
Cristiano Ronaldo's 981st goal helps Al Nassr win as Al Ain go top of AFC Champions League

report.text: Cristiano Ronaldo scored his 981st professional goal, across club and country, as Al Nassr beat Neftchi 3-1 in the AFC Champions League Elite on Monday. The strike keeps him on course for his target of 1,000 career goals. The goal came amid a row over his future with Portugal. The 41-year-old has been provisionally suspended by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after leaving the national camp during the UEFA Nations League, and disciplinary proceedings have been opened against him. His rift with head coach Jorge Jesus has deepened. THE MATCH Angelo Gabriel put Al Nassr ahead in the 33rd minute, and Ronaldo added the second nine minutes later. Alisher Odilov pulled one back for Neftchi in the 51st minute. An own goal by Anvarjon Gofurov in the 78th minute gave Al Nassr a two-goal cushion, and the scoreline stayed the same until the end. After the game, Ronaldo posted on Instagram: “Important win tonight. We keep building.” THE SUSPENSION The FPF’s disciplinary council has suspended Ronaldo on a non-automatic basis and classified the case as “urgent”. According to Goal.com, this is the first sanction against him while the investigation is pending, before any final penalty.

report.text: West Indies' Keemo Paul, left, celebrate with captain Shai Hope the wicket of India's Sanju Samson during the fourth T20 cricket match between India and West Indies in Hyderabad, India, Wednesday, Oct. 14, 2026. (AP Photo/Mahesh Kumar A.) HYDERABAD, India (AP) — Shai Hope set a West Indies record by reaching 102 not out as West Indies beat India by 24 runs Wednesday in the fourth cricket T20 to level the five-match series at 2-2. Hope hit nine sixes and four fours in his third T20 century – the most for a West Indies batter – as the visitors piled up 247-3 in 20 overs. India had won the toss and opted to bowl. It was the second-highest first innings total in T20s against India, trailing England’s 257-3 in Southampton this year. In reply, Sanju Samson hit 56 off 23 balls but India was down to 130-5 and the chase never took off. It finished with 223 in 19.3 overs. Keemo Paul picked 5-41 for his second five-wicket haul in T20s. Put into bat, Hope gave West Indies a flying by putting on 52 off 26 balls with Jewel Andrew (21). reports.headline: George Russell calls Red Bull "the team to beat" in F1, but Kimi Antonelli adds a key caveat
Fans can't get enough of Max Verstappen's floral race boots after Singapore win

report.text: Formula 1’s Asian triple-header has gone particularly well for Max Verstappen. The Red Bull driver finished 0.196 seconds behind Russell in Baku before going on to claim convincing victories in Malaysia and Singapore. On both sides of the equation – at Red Bull and Mercedes – this is linked to major upgrades introduced during the recent triple-header. Red Bull brought its final major package for the RB22 to Baku and immediately made a significant step forward. Read Also: Formula 1Who slept best last night: Max Verstappen At Mercedes, the reality has proved more complicated. The Silver Arrows introduced their long-awaited upgrade for the W17 in Malaysia, but it did not immediately provide the answers they were looking for – partly because of the unusual characteristics of the Sepang International Circuit, with its extremely rough tarmac. In Singapore, Russell ran the old spec while Antonelli used the new one to gather comparative data and find answers. The preliminary conclusion is that the upgrade does indeed offer greater potential, but the operating window in which that potential can be unlocked is extremely narrow.
